clusters.name: Your stepfather Desmond moving in and your father's separation from Bettina, 1987
clusters.reason: Around 1987, when you were in early secondary school, three shifts pile up: you found distance between yourself and Desmond, you moved closer to your father despite the tension, and you made the chess squad but felt out of your depth. Your stepparents' separation sat in those months as well. No other family member's shifts show then, and these are yours alone.

clusters.name: Your grandfather Gordon's death and your move through secondary school, 1989–1994
clusters.reason: From early 1989 through 1994, shifts pile up around your grandfather Gordon's death in June 1991 and the upheaval in your household: your father's grandfather Clifford came back into the family that year, your family moved to Hollin Road, you developed late nights and grew anxious at school, you dropped chess and debate, your sister Tara was born in 1990, you let your mother fill in your college forms and fused with Rafe at the conservatory, you injured your wrist and fell into using drugs and low functioning. Your grandmother Winifred had thyroid surgery not long after his death. These shifts lay close together across the period, and the settled point comes as you found your drive again with the exchange to Portugal in early 1994.

clusters.name: Your relationship with Joelle and your performing peak, 1998–1999
clusters.reason: Around 1998 and 1999, you began a relationship with Joelle, your insomnia worsened before concerts, and you played the best you ever had, winning competitions. You separated by mid-1999 and started therapy with Victor afterward. These shifts are yours alone, and no other family member's shows in these months.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Winifred's bowel cancer and your move away from home, 2001–2004
clusters.reason: From 2001 through early 2004, you lost steam for performing, your anxiety rose and functioning fell, you had a disastrous audition in your home town, your grandmother Winifred was found to have bowel cancer in 2001 or 2002 and died in February 2004. Around the same time you distanced from your parents, left Thornbury for Gull Harbour, met Marisol in early 2003, moved to Fenwick with her, and split within months. You sank into deep depression, could not face your family, relied on friends instead, and only climbed out once you returned to therapy with Victor and your mother helped with costs. Your grandmother spent her final months in your parents' home while you were distant from them. The shifts run close together across these years and settle as you began swimming and returned to your therapist in January 2004, the same month you dropped in on your grandmother hung over on your way to the airport.

clusters.name: Your grandmother Lorna's death and your move to nursing school, 2008
clusters.reason: In 2008, your grandmother Lorna died in January, your grandfather Clifford died that year as well, and you began nursing school in Marlow Sound in September. In the months between, you were too drained for conversation with your mother at Alder Creek, she pressed you to visit against your wishes, you kept the door shut on her when she arrived, you stopped speaking to her altogether when you left for school, and you cut off for roughly a year. Your aunt Imogen had a stroke in January 2009 with months of rehabilitation. These shifts gather around your move away and the losses in your extended family, and the silence with your mother held through the first year of school.

clusters.name: Your marriage to Wren and upheaval in her family, 2017–2019
clusters.reason: From your marriage in March 2017 through October 2019, shifts pile up around changes in both families: you saw your mother a bit less once Wren came along, your cousin Alice was diagnosed with multiple sclerosis in October 2017, your sister Tara had a baby on the way in autumn 2019, and through 2019 your partner's mother Frances retired and the family gathered at the lake house. Around that same time Wren grew swamped with one thing after another, her anxiety and symptom rose while functioning fell, you overfunctioned laying out a plan to settle her, she and her father and brother spoke all day with nothing happening to one that the others didn't hear, your sleep worsened at family occasions and you felt you didn't belong, you were awake from the small hours at the lake weekend with no more sleep, and your job steadied and paid well. Wren's anxiety eased once the weekend had a plan. Your cousin Imogen's memory loss worsened and she lashed out when muddled. These shifts run close together through 2019, and the settled point comes as you learned to aim for shorter, more regular calls with your mother rather than letting distance pile up.

periods.name: the year I left home
periods.words: The first is the year I left home: I went off to the conservatory, hurt my wrist in the first term and couldn't play, dropped out and drifted at my mother's place, then spent a bleak spell at the community college shooting pool every night until an exchange in Portugal snapped me out of it and I tore through the rest of my coursework.

periods.name: the long slump
periods.words: The second is the long slump, roughly ages 27 to 29, when nothing at home felt right, I moved to Gull Harbour away from nearly everyone I knew, then followed Marisol to Fenwick, and when that fell apart I went under, a depression I only really climbed out of after nursing school.
